required_facts.claim: These workshops require participants to have access to cloud resources such as AWS.
required_facts.source_evidence: These workshops require participants to have access to cloud resources such as AWS.

required_facts.claim: This is okay when people come prepared, but often it’s not the case.

required_facts.claim: This happened when Exasol, a database company, asked me to run a workshop for them.
required_facts.source_evidence: This happened when Exasol, a database company, asked me to run a workshop for them.

required_facts.claim: They released a new version of their database, Exasol Personal.
required_facts.source_evidence: They released a new version of their database, Exasol Personal.

required_facts.claim: It’s normally a paid service, but this edition runs in your own AWS account.
required_facts.source_evidence: It’s normally a paid service, but this edition runs in your own AWS account.

required_facts.claim: You need an account and a few permissions, then you can create a cluster and use it from your laptop.
required_facts.source_evidence: You need an account and a few permissions, then you can create a cluster and use it from your laptop.

required_facts.claim: For me, it was very easy to set it up.

required_facts.claim: But then I started thinking about how to make it scale to 50-60 workshop participants, who will most likely be unprepared.
required_facts.source_evidence: But then I started thinking about how to make it scale to 50-60 workshop participants, who will most likely be unprepared.

required_facts.claim: So I needed to find a way for the participants to provision resources in my AWS account without giving them my AWS keys.
required_facts.source_evidence: So I needed to find a way for the participants to provision resources in my AWS account without giving them my AWS keys.

required_facts.claim: The solution I found turned out to be useful not only for workshops, but also for coding agents.
